why: How one `Effect::RequestFileOpen` becomes real bytes in a guest, stated once for every renderer. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END: the wgpu door had no `request-file-open` case in `wireEffectToFriendly` at all (`unmapped effect "request-file-open" dropped`, measured on 6118), its shell read `requestFileOpen` out of a MUTATION payload no producer emits, its wasm32 `request_file_open` was a stub returning nothing, and — had it returned something — it dispatched `{json, payload}` in ONE unchunked invocation while React dispatched `{payload, name, chunk, chunkCount}` per chunk. Four spellings of one journey. This fixture is the one spelling: the wire shapes the effect really arrives in, the chunk slicing both hosts owe the guest, and the exact argument envelope one chunk is dispatched with.
importChunkBytesWhy: `GUEST_CONTIGUOUS_REQUEST_CEILING_BYTES / 2` (65 536 / 2). Derived in both twins from the guest's own per-request contiguous ceiling, never restated as a literal — this number is here only so a fixture reader can check the twins agree on it.

wireCases.why: The shape the ACTOR boundary hands a renderer door: a WIT `option<string>` as its tagged variant record. These are the exact `generation3d` values recorded on 6118 — request id 131, the accept filter the artifact derives from its own importable formats, `dataUrl`, and `importDocument` as the verb the shell re-dispatches.

The shape jco's DIRECT binding hands over for the same field — the bare value. Both are real on the same field, which is exactly how `download-media-export.encoding` was lost; one decoder must read both.

The WIT record spells these `read-as`/`import-action`; jco lowers them to camelCase, but a boundary that hands the record through verbatim keeps the kebab spelling — the same two-real-shapes situation `download-media-export.mime-type` already carries a reader for. A door that reads only one of them re-dispatches nothing, which is indistinguishable from a cancelled picker.
`read_as: None` means the shell hands back the file's own text rather than a data URL, and `multiple` is a plain WIT `bool`. `process3d`/`home` pick this shape.

W0 nested every `req`-bearing effect's payload into its own `…-params` record. A door that reads this effect FLAT gets an empty `importAction` and re-dispatches nothing — the same defect `dispatch-action` already carries a note about. An effect with no `params` therefore decodes to empty strings rather than to a guessed top-level read.

chunkCases.why: A picked empty file is a real pick. One chunk of zero bytes, never zero chunks, or the guest is never told the run happened.
The probe's own file, well under the ceiling: exactly one chunk whose envelope names itself 0 of 1.
chunkCases.payload:
solid probe
facet normal 0 0 1
endsolid probe
chunks:
solid probe
facet normal 0 0 1
endsolid probe

chunkCases.why: A payload of exactly `importChunkBytes` ASCII characters is ONE chunk — the bound is inclusive.
One character more is two chunks, the second carrying exactly one character.

`ō` is 2 UTF-8 bytes and 1 UTF-16 unit. Counted in code units the page would overrun the guest's byte cap; counted in bytes the last character that no longer fits starts the next page, and no page ever ends mid-code-point. 16 385 of them are 32 770 bytes, so the first page holds 16 384 and the second holds 1.
An emoji is 4 UTF-8 bytes and 2 UTF-16 units — the case a UTF-16 slice overruns by 2×. 8 193 of them are 32 772 bytes: 8 192 fit the first page exactly, the last starts the second.

argumentCases.why: The shape every small pick takes, and the only one `generation3d`'s session-free `importDocument` entry point admits. `chunk`/`chunkCount` are INTEGERS: the guest decodes them as `u32` and `FromValue`'s unsigned arm refuses a float, which is how an integer widened on a lossy JSON hop kills the whole dispatch.
argumentCases.name: probe-triangle.stl

argumentCases.why: A chunked run names its own position. The guest's staging refuses a gap rather than resuming into bytes nobody can account for, so the position is the contract, not a hint.
argumentCases.name: nakagin.json

argumentCases.why: `index`/`total` are added ONLY when the picker was opened with `multiple`, so a single-file pick's args are byte-for-byte the pre-fan-out shape.
argumentCases.name: b.stl

integerArgumentsWhy: `chunk`, `chunkCount`, `index` and `total` MUST reach the guest as exact unsigned integers. Both twins mint them as integer carriers (Rust `Number::UInt`, TypeScript `packUInt`) rather than letting them widen onto a float on a JSON hop — the defect that took every wgpu dispatch down once the view state first carried a `u64` (`📓️wgpu-end-to-end-verification-2026-09-14.md` §A).
